Proposition 3.1 (Well-posedness and stationarity of the conditional phase space process) . For every fixed $y,\widetilde{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and initial phase space point $(x_{0},p_{0})$ , the event-driven dynamics in Algorithm 1 , with the reference point fixed at $\widetilde{x}$ , defines a unique non-explosive, time-homogeneous Markov process. The phase space measure $\nu_{\eta,y}$ is stationary for this process. In particular, the returned position $x_{\pi}$ is well-defined almost surely.

Proposition 3.2 (Reversibility of the conditional half-turn kernel) . For every $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ , let $\mathcal{H}_{y}$ be the Markov kernel on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ induced by Algorithm 1 ; thus $\mathcal{H}_{y}(x,\cdot)$ is the law of the returned position $x_{\pi}$ for input $(x,y)$ . Then $\mathcal{H}_{y}$ is reversible with respect to $\pi_{\eta}^{X\mid Y=y}$ .

Proposition A.1 (Path reversal, invariance, and the $L^{2}$ semigroup) . Let $(\mathsf{T}_{t}^{y,\widetilde{x}})_{t\geq 0}$ be the Markov transition operators of the process constructed in Proposition 3.1 . Proposition A.2 (Joint measurability and augmented space half-turn operator) . The family of conditional half-turn kernels $(\mathcal{H}_{y})_{y\in\mathbb{R}^{d}}$ admits a version, again denoted by $\mathcal{H}_{y}(x,\mathrm{d}x^{\prime})$ , such that $(y,x)\mapsto\mathcal{H}_{y}(x,A)$ is Borel measurable for every Borel set $A\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}$ . Consequently, $(\mathsf{H}f)(x,y)\coloneqq\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}f(x^{\prime},y)\,\mathcal{H}_{y}(x,\mathrm{d}x^{\prime})$ (A.9) defines a self-adjoint Markov contraction on $L^{2}(\pi_{\eta})$ .
